title: Copying a layer and pasting it gives the copy its own name
goal: Copy a layer and paste it and you get two rows in the layers list reading the exact same word, with no way to tell which is which until you rename one. Duplicating the same layer instead already reads "Hero banner copy", so the two ways of making a copy disagree.
notes: Verified in the probe on 2026-09-03: drop Hero banner.png, copyLayer, pasteLayer, two rows both read "Hero banner". EditorState.pasteLayer sets layer.name = transfer.layer.name, which deliberately undoes the " copy" that Layer.duplicated appends, and PhotonzDocument.uniquelyNamed only numbers names built from LayerNaming.autoStems, which a file-derived name is not. The duplicate path (nameDuplicates -> LayerNaming.copyName) is the shape to match. Sibling of two-pictures-with-the-same-name-get-told-apart-i, which fixed the same defect for placing a file twice.
acceptance: Copying a layer and pasting it leaves two rows with different names
The pasted row is named the same way duplicating that layer names it
A name a person typed is never changed on the layer that was already there

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the mock-free question is what a paste should be called when it lands somewhere the original is not (another document, or after a cut). Always adding "copy" would rename a cut-and-pasted layer behind the user's back, so the rule is the one PlacedImageNaming already uses: nothing is renamed until there is something to tell it apart from. In the same-document case that is identical to what duplicate does, which is what the task asks for.

TDD: Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PastedLayerNamingTests.swift (8 tests) written first and red, then LayerNaming.pastedName(of:taken:) added. One test asserts paste and duplicateLayer agree name for name across app-written, person-typed and already-copied names.
EditorState.pasteLayer no longer restores transfer.layer.name; it asks LayerNaming.pastedName against the names in the document it is landing in. Shared file, so Current and Next both have it.

Verified live in the probe with Scripts/playtest/pasted-layer-name-walk.json: Hero banner, Hero banner copy, Hero banner copy 2, duplicate then gives Hero banner copy 3, and a hand-typed "Renamed Layer" is untouched while its copy reads "Renamed Layer copy". Screen Recording granted, real capture at queue/audits/2026-09-04-pasted-layer-name.png. Scripts/test.sh: 2870 tests pass.
Review of the built thing: repeated pastes all land at the same 16,16 offset and stack invisibly. Left alone (naming was the task) and filed as a-second-paste-lands-where-you-can-see-it.
